records.statement: Binance's October 30 Security Incident Update #2 reports more than $6.34B company funds set aside, $5B held in exact affected token assets and remaining relevant token purchases through market/OTC channels, but no token-level XRP allocation, purchase quantity, execution venue, fill or settlement was disclosed.

At the 2026-10-31T05:05Z cutoff, no later official announcement verifying withdrawal resumption or the initial post-incident PoR snapshot was found. The approximately 12-hour initial snapshot target from the Oct30 19:33Z update is 2026-10-31 07:33Z; the approximately 34-hour withdrawal target is 2026-11-01 05:33Z; results were expected by Nov2. These are targets, not completed events.

Kodexius reports $739.41M XRP OI across seven contracts at 00:14Z Oct31; TradRadar reports $1.85B across seven exchanges at 23:20Z Oct30. Different contract/venue universes and observation times prevent averaging or treating the difference as a market move. Preserve provider-specific series until contract-level coverage is reconciled.

Investing.com daily candles show Oct29 XRP -6.84% and Oct30 +1.22%, but the Oct29 daily interval includes the Binance incident and other market events. Daily OHLC cannot identify incident causality; synchronized BTC/ETH controls, event-level spot depth, venue-specific derivatives and exact incident timestamps are required.

GitHub code search and targeted file reads identified multiple scheduled write-capable workflows, but this is not a complete permission audit of every workflow, action, repository ruleset or effective token setting. The first open-PR page returned 100 items; the last full open-PR count of 168 is from 04:28Z and was not refreshed. Some workflows have contents:write but their exact mutation target/run was not established.

PR #1395 only disables the scheduler-tick queue writer/dispatcher if approved and merged. PR #1392 proposes read-only cross-analysis, signal-accuracy and telemetry behavior but remains draft/unmerged and does not address all other scheduled writers. Main remains exposed until each relevant change is reviewed and approved; no merge was authorized.
